PER01 — Always make the current merchant or platform context visible. A user holding both relationships exercises each separately. Changing context does not import rights from the previous context.

PER02 — Deny unauthorized actions consistently regardless of how the action is reached. Disabling a visible control alone is insufficient. Denied attempts do not cause external effects and remain reviewable without exposing another merchant's data.

PER03 — Merchant membership invitations identify merchant, recipient and offered role. Expired/revoked/wrong-recipient invitations cannot be accepted. An Admin must remain available; recovery is explicit and audited.

PER04 — Platform support can inspect merchant identity, member administration, freshness/error summaries and aggregate queue health. Redacted diagnostic information is the MVP support path. Impersonation, contact-level support browsing and merchant-action overrides are EXCLUDED from MVP.

PER05 — An invitation or support request cannot let platform staff silently add themselves as Merchant Admin. Recovery of an Admin membership requires verification of the legitimate merchant representative, records the authorizing party and blocks self-grant. Verification method is OP02, a launch decision.

PER08 — Exceptional outreach after the same contact objective's three attempts is not an Admin permission in MVP. Admin can review unfinished work and request a future policy change; higher contact limits need explicit owner approval changing OD04.

PER06 — Each consequential request records the acting Merchant Admin and exact reviewed intent. For supported connected actions, Admin authorizes/initiates in OpsHub and OpsHub executes/reconciles the external result; Operator/platform authority cannot invoke that effect. Manual execution is an attributed fallback exception. Admin may approve their own request; mandatory dual approval remains deferred. Material recipient/items/value/action-scope edits invalidate approval and require a new Admin decision.
PER07 — Uncertain imported callers/confirmers remain source claims, separate from authenticated recording/importing users. Never relabel historical free text as verified actor identity.

KPI01 — Display business meaning, numerator/denominator counts, population/grain, time basis and interval, exclusions/unknowns, source coverage, definition version and calculated/as-of time. A compact visible explanation may link to full contributing records; the value must never appear without its denominator/window qualification. Export carries the same contract.

KPI02 — Zero denominator is **N/A**, never 0% or 100%. Missing input is not zero. Distinguish zero measured activity, partial period, pending final outcome, incomplete source coverage and unresolved mapping. Ratios are computed from unrounded counts/amounts, with presentation rounding only.

KPI03 — Proposed merchant-local calendar: daily/calendar month/custom intervals and Monday–Sunday week; interval boundaries and timezone always named. A current partial week is compared only against an explicit equal-length prior interval, or against a labeled complete period with warning. This calendar/cohort choice is OP07, not part of the approved OD05 formula.

KPI04 — Cohort dates and as-of dates differ. Late outcomes/corrections can revise a cohort's rate; retained/exported summaries identify as-of and input revision. Ageing/backlog uses current merchant time rather than a stale export's last date; imported date-only/unknown-zone values retain precision uncertainty.

KPI05 — For known population with some pending outcomes, display the final-outcome ratio plus pending/unknown counts. If source completeness is unknown or unmapped records could change numerator/finality, label the known-population result **provisional** with uncovered count/unknown coverage; never call it merchant-wide performance. If the subject population or denominator cannot be reliably formed, withhold the ratio as **unavailable** and show reasons.

CON01 — Admin connects/authorizes the intended merchant source context and reviews source ownership, capability availability and mappings. Operators may inspect/refresh permitted read evidence without gaining connection configuration or consequential execution rights. Show not configured, ready, limited capability, failed/unavailable and stale/partial states with affected work.

CON02 — Connected new/changed orders, shipments and applicable spend arrive/update without routine user copy/paste. Show last successful receipt, provider as-of/coverage, recent failure and relevant time basis. Refresh/readiness targets are product acceptance values in OP08/OP13; Gentry's ten-minute UI claim is not adopted as a proved SLA or a mechanism.

CON03 — Repeated connected observations cannot create extra orders, contacts, outbound shipments or costs. Corrections preserve revisions/provenance. Source ingest/update alone cannot trigger booking/cancellation/replacement without the separately required Admin decision.

ING01 — Select merchant and source ownership explicitly. Preserve original identifier strings, account/source scope, capture/input provenance and coverage interval. Identical order numbers/tracking/SKU labels in another merchant must never cross-link.

ING02 — Review connection mappings/coverage and preview fallback file fields, date/number/currency interpretation, object grain, likely additions/updates and duplicate/conflict/unmatched counts. Operator uses approved mappings; Merchant Admin reviews changes. Do not infer native uniqueness from a single export.

ING03 — Validate required identity/merchant/format and supported episode constraints before acceptance. Report each rejected/held row with actionable cause and safe row locator; preserve original values. Unclear phone matches cannot choose among orders/customers. Four long item descriptions or multi-digit quantities cannot be silently truncated to Gentry's historical parser limits.

ING04 — Account for every submitted input row as accepted, repeated, rejected or held/unmatched; identify whether one accepted row updates an existing object. A mixed file can accept independent safe rows only when the user sees the exact accepted/rejected scope. Invalid dependent groups are held together rather than leaving an apparently complete order with missing required parts. Failed new ingestion preserves prior accepted data.

ING05 — Re-importing an identical accepted file under the same mapping/source cannot create new orders, shipment episodes, contact attempts or external actions. A source correction is a new observed revision with before/after/provenance, not a duplicate event. Distinct genuinely evidenced contacts remain distinct even when their text/timestamps match. Ambiguous event deduplication is held for review; the MVP supported-contact-import contract needs OP13 approval.

ING06 — Keep contradictory source assertions visible. The approved source selection/manual override determines a displayed working view only for the named concept; it does not destroy alternate claims or fabricate physical/financial events. Importing a cancellation/payment/tag assertion never executes that business action externally.

ING07 — Show received/accepted time, source-reported coverage/as-of, last successful update, last failure and affected population separately. Connected-source freshness follows the qualified product target; manual fallback is labeled with its exception reason and merchant refresh dependence. Do not present fallback receipt as restored connection health.

ING08 — Source gaps, unknown statuses and multiple/repeated/partial historical episodes enter review with their original observations. OD06 remains the supported OpsHub order model; historical reverse legs retain purpose. Do not discard a second leg to satisfy the MVP or invent a replacement identity without evidence.

ING09 — Imported aggregate contact/courier counters remain summaries. No generated attempt chronology, authenticated historical actor or consent timestamp is fabricated. Seven Gentry call-before-order anomalies remain contradictions until source evidence explains them.

ING10 — A sync/file result cannot claim success for unavailable sources. Disconnecting or failing a source leaves last accepted data labeled stale/partial; it does not reset counts to zero or remove unresolved work. Data refresh should update current queue/KPI projections with a traceable new as-of.

ACT01 — Operator prepares → Admin reviews exact intent and authorizes/initiates in OpsHub → OpsHub performs the supported external action → returned identifier/result and later status are received/reconciled → required work closes only under OD03. Track not started/pending/succeeded/failed/unknown per effect; provider acknowledgement is not physical completion. Record Admin authority and OpsHub execution origin separately from source/recording actor.

ACT02 — Only one current intent may be actionable for the same booking/recovery objective. Competing Admins, repeated submissions, delayed results and recovery cannot authorize duplicate effects. A changed intent requires reapproval. Unknown first effect blocks connected re-execution and manual fallback execution until reconciled; no blind retry/rollback claim. Successful replacement creation plus failed booking retains the known new order and pending booking, not another replacement.

ACT03 — Denial must prevent the connected external action, not merely hide a button. Platform authority never authorizes merchant execution. Reported unauthorized/duplicate effects from independently operated provider accounts remain discrepancies, not retrospectively approved. Native refunds, arbitrary payment changes and unqualified courier operations are not silently added by OD08.

FB01 — Fallback is available for temporary integration outage, provider-unsupported action/input, incomplete onboarding or reviewed safe exception. Show reason, missing capability, current request/result knowledge and responsible actor. Operator may prepare/import approved evidence; consequential external execution and result acceptance remain Admin-controlled.

FB02 — Handover to external execution requires a known not-started intent or a reliably evidenced no-effect result under the qualified action contract. A timeout, failed refresh, missing record or unsupported absence lookup is not proof of nonexecution. Unknown earlier effect remains blocked/open. Safe handover makes the prior path nonactionable and records Admin/reason/negative-evidence basis; capture fallback provider reference/time/outcome. Missing positive result evidence stays unknown. OpsHub cannot prevent independent provider-account activity; fallback must demonstrate correct authority.

FB03 — When a connection recovers, reconcile fallback evidence with connected records without duplicates or overwriting disputes. Show connection restored separately from fallback completion. Imports/exports and off-platform work are not the normal route for an available integrated source.

EXP01 — Export matches the requested merchant, filters, population, period and as-of. Orders, contact cases/events and shipment populations retain their named grain. Carry original source references, unknown/blank distinctions, relevant definition and caveats. Do not silently export all calls when a period subset was selected.

EXP02 — Operator exports omit direct contact details and free-text contact narratives. Admin contact-bearing export is a separate explicit choice showing affected scope, with audit. Platform exports contain scoped administration/aggregate diagnostics only. See OP12 for retention/distribution policy.

EXP03 — Preserve historical Gentry labels/definition provenance for a future comparison pack. Normalized OpsHub metrics appear alongside documented differences; no requirement to reproduce missing archived narrative inputs or workbook layout. [AC12](11-mvp-acceptance-criteria.md#ac12--legacy-comparison-readiness) defines comparison readiness.

COM01 — Each merchant has an explicit assigned plan/tier concept and commercial status, with current effective dates, authorizing platform actor and history. MVP can use one manually assigned pilot offering. Plan names/packaging and exact prices remain **TBD — COMMERCIAL DECISION**. No price, payment processor, invoice/payment entities or billing architecture is selected.

COM02 — A designated Merchant Admin is the billing owner/contact. Other Operators see availability/service notices without unrestricted commercial or contact details. Platform staff can administer the offering/status without obtaining merchant operational authority.

COM03 — Proposed commercial states: evaluation/trial (only if offered), active, overdue/review-required, suspended and closed. Service activation, onboarding readiness and commercial standing are displayed separately. A merchant can be commercially active yet have incomplete input readiness.

COM04 — Proposed state changes are manually authorized in MVP. Overdue does not automatically suspend; trial expiry, grace period, charges and exact transitions require OP11 approval. Trial is optional, with duration **TBD — COMMERCIAL DECISION**; no hidden default trial or automatic charge.

COM05 — Subscription/plan status shows what is permitted, effective period and how the Admin can request renewal/reactivation. Failed commercial administration does not mark merchant operations completed or discard data.

COM06 — Suspension **must not destroy** merchant operational data, relationships, imported evidence or audit/history. Proposed behavior is read-only access for active Merchant Admins, existing-record exports and clear recovery notice; block new operational writes/ingestion/consequential requests until reactivation. Operator visibility and emergency continuity need OP11 approval before pilot.

COM07 — Pending requests/actions remain identifiable with their last evidence and responsible party. No automatic cancellation/refund/booking is caused by suspension or closure. Any external action already initiated is retained as succeeded/failed/unknown according to evidence, never relabeled as undone.

COM08 — Reactivation restores permitted access and preserved history, recomputes current attention with explicit freshness and prevents catch-up contact attempts from being scheduled tightly together. It does not fabricate input updates from the suspended period.

COM09 — Administrative closure is not destructive deletion. Retention/export/recovery policy requires OP12 approval. Account closure cannot authorize deletion without a separately approved product/legal retention policy.

COM10 — Entitlements may identify supported modules/member/input volume limits only when approved commercial packaging actually requires them. No detailed usage meter, overage billing or invented order quota is required for MVP. A limit must be visible before the user performs affected work; reaching it cannot silently drop data or deny access to retained history.

COM11 — A human billing/support process may maintain commercial records; OpsHub need not process payments in MVP. It must not present “paid invoice” or verified settlement without evidence. Subscription status is not a customer-order payment assertion.

AUD01 — Consequential cancellation, booking, replacement, supported financial-action evidence and significant policy/source-authority changes retain: **what happened, when, initiating user, merchant, prior/new state where relevant, reviewed request/approval, outcome/failure/unknown and source/result evidence**. Distinguish requester, approving/initiating Merchant Admin, OpsHub connected execution origin, provider result and recording actor. New manual-fallback completion identifies Admin executor, exception reason, handover and accepted evidence; unverifiable results stay under review. Unknown historical actors/time remain unknown.

AUD02 — Audit onboarding/account/service/plan changes, invitations/membership/platform grants, source mappings, imports/repeats/rejections, exports, corrections, case closure/reopen, collection attestations and attempts-exhausted decisions. Denied consequential requests and attempted scope violations are reviewable without exposing unauthorized payloads.

AUD03 — Past available assertions and audit entries cannot be silently overwritten through ordinary editing. Correction appends attributable reason/prior/new/source/time and updates the current working view. Displayed history must explain what was known versus what changed; no fabricated older revision is required.

AUD04 — Consequential approval identifies exact reviewed intent. Result history distinguishes each required external effect: not started, succeeded, failed or unknown. “Approved” is never displayed as “completed”; duplicate/partial effects remain visible until reconciled. Material intent change requires fresh approval.

AUD05 — A source-reported caller/confirmer/payment/cash-out label remains source-reported. Authenticated recording/import user is a separate attributed actor. Fee components and aggregate are alternative views unless explicitly reconciled; source Paid does not prove bank settlement/customer refund.

AUD06 — Ordinary merchant users can inspect their operational history; Admin sees merchant administrative/action evidence. Platform sees scoped administrative audit and redacted diagnostics. Platform assignment is not permission to read customer contact payloads or execute merchant business actions.

TR01 — Quality attention explains affected record/source/rule, impact and permitted next action. Missing fields block only the capability whose prerequisite they invalidate. Missing margin/cost context does not block calling or canonical revenue/spend ROAS; incomplete attributed revenue/spend does qualify/withhold ROAS. Unresolved recipient/order identity blocks confident booking. Product/SKU/outcome/ad-allocation quality is required MVP trust, not deferred quality work.

TR02 — KPI/report exports retain completeness, unknown/excluded population and as-of. Incompatible source coverage/definitions are not compared without a visible qualification. Historical Gentry CLEAN/CAUTION/BLOCKED intent becomes user-visible complete/provisional/unavailable behavior, not a claim that its scripts enforced all gates.

TR03 — Review of a shared summary is attributable to the reviewed content/as-of. Editing it invalidates an earlier review claim. MVP sharing is a manual Admin responsibility; OpsHub does not send customer/owner communications automatically.

TR04 — Customer identifiers, raw contact exports and narratives must not leak through platform diagnostics or general summaries. Contact-bearing export is explicit Admin scope. Source originals and historical evidence names remain unchanged.

TR05 — Logical merchant isolation applies to every view, search, association, queue, metric, import, export and history. Same User or repeated phone/order number across merchants never permits cross-merchant linkage/access. Platform health overview contains only permitted aggregates/admin data, including redacted connection/analytics-input readiness.

TR06 — Retention, post-closure access, diagnostic visibility and supported security/session policy need explicit owner approval before pilot (OP12). This PRD requires authenticated access, role/scope denial, access removal and audit; it chooses no enforcement mechanism or compliance certification.

TR07 — Connected receipt success is separate from source coverage, action acknowledgement, final effect and restored health. Product/ROAS exports retain item/outcome/attribution/revenue/spend definitions and input revision; partial or unmapped data cannot be presented as complete product performance. Fallback/source reconciliation preserves earlier available claims without double-counting allocations or external effects.

**IM04:** new verified provider account binding requires ownership review.
